Affinity-graph embedding methods (such as Laplacian Eigenmaps, LLE, Isomap, and spectral embeddings) build a pairwise affinity or similarity matrix over all n nodes. Storing that matrix takes O(n^2) memory, and it is often dense. The main computational bottleneck is the eigendecomposition (or other spectral solve) of this n×n matrix, which costs roughly O(n^3) time in the naive case. Constructing the pairwise affinities and shortest-path or neighbourhood computations add further quadratic costs. Together these make the methods impractical as the number of nodes grows, and approximations such as sparse graphs, landmarks, or randomized eigensolvers are typically used to address this.
